title: Network Attorney Filing Standard — Suit Conditions and Authorization Validity for Legal Forwarding Agreements Matters
content:
On a matter forwarded under the Legal Forwarding Agreements, the attorney's filing of suit is recorded with the filing date, the court's case number and the court the suit was filed in (small claims, limited civil or general civil). The conditions on that filing are set out below.

## Filing conditions

**(1) Pre-filing conditions.** A suit is filed only where the client's programme files suits, and only:

- after the programme's number of attorney demand letters has been sent, and after the programme's waiting period in calendar days following the last of those letters;
- after a skip trace, where the programme requires a skip trace before filing; and
- with a servicemember status affidavit ready, where the programme requires that affidavit.

**(2) Authorization validity.** A suit is filed only when the handling date is no later than the authorization validity counted from the matter's authorization date. The authorization validity is the programme's authorization validity in calendar days, the day after the authorization date being day one and the last day included; an expired authorization needs a new one.

**(3) Suit fee.** The programme's suit fee is charged to the client on filing.

**(4) Court.** The court is chosen by balance, small claims being used up to the state's small-claims limit.

**(5) One suit.** A matter carries one suit.

## Authorization validity, step by step

| Element | Fixed by |
|---|---|
| Anchor | the authorization date recorded on the matter in Ridgeline's records |
| Day one | the calendar day after the authorization date |
| Length | the programme's authorization validity, in calendar days |
| Last day | included — a suit may still be filed on it |
| After the last day | the authorization has expired; a new one is needed before a suit is filed |

### Boundary cases on hypothetical dates

The dates and lengths are invented to show the count.

| Authorization date | Validity length | Last day | Filing on the last day | Filing the day after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 May | 60 days | 9 July (11–31 May are days 1–21, June brings day 51, 9 July is day 60) | allowed | not allowed; a new authorization is needed |
| 10 May | 90 days | 8 August (31 May is day 21, 30 June day 51, 31 July day 82, 8 August day 90) | allowed | not allowed; a new authorization is needed |

## Pre-filing conditions as a table

| Condition | When it applies | If it is not satisfied |
|---|---|---|
| Programme files suits | always | no suit is filed |
| Demand letters sent and waiting period after the last one passed | always | no suit is filed |
| Skip trace done | where the programme requires it | no suit is filed |
| Servicemember status affidavit ready | where the programme requires it | no suit is filed |
| Authorization within its validity | always | no suit is filed on the expired authorization |

### Hypothetical illustrations

- A programme that sends two demand letters with a 30-day waiting period: the waiting period runs from the second letter. A filing ten days after the second letter is too early; a filing forty-five days after it is past the waiting period.
- A programme that files no suits: no suit is filed on any of its matters, whatever the balance.
- A matter that already carries a suit: no second suit is filed on it.
